task.description:
Register the "Preview This" feature as a global CommandManager command so it appears in the Configure Shortcuts dialog and can be assigned a keyboard shortcut.
Currently, "Preview This" is only a local QAction created in the RowArea context menu (xshrowviewer.cpp:1367). It calls RowArea::onPreviewThis() which sets both the start and stop play-range markers to the right-clicked row (m_row), effectively pinning preview to a single frame.
Because it is never registered with CommandManager::define(), it does not appear in the ShortcutPopup tree and cannot receive a shortcut binding.
The fix requires: 1. Adding a new command identifier MI_PreviewThis to menubarcommandids.h. 2. Registering it via createMenuXsheetAction() in MainWindow::defineActions(). 3. Creating a MenuItemHandler subclass that performs the same "set both markers to current frame" logic, using TApp::instance()->getCurrentFrame()->getFrame() instead of the context-menu m_row. 4. Updating the context menu in RowArea::contextMenuEvent() to use the CommandManager action so the shortcut label shows up in the menu.

Investigate how OpenToonz shortcuts are wired: command IDs, registration, CommandManager, ShortcutPopup, and how existing xsheet context menu commands (e.g. MI_InsertSceneFrame) are made shortcuttable.

input.file: CommandManager class defining command registration, Node, define(), getAction().
MainWindow::defineActions() — registration site for all shortcuttable commands. MainWindow::createAction() / createMenuXsheetAction() — how commands are defined.
ShortcutTree and ShortcutPopup — UI that reads CommandManager to populate the shortcut configuration tree.
RowArea::contextMenuEvent() — where "Preview This" is defined as a local QAction. RowArea::onPreviewThis() — implementation at line 1534.
RowArea class declaration including onPreviewThis() slot.

steps.step: Inspected CommandManager (menubarcommand.h): singleton with define(), getAction(), setShortcut(), loadShortcuts(). Commands are registered by calling define() with an id string, CommandType enum, default shortcut, and a QAction pointer.
Inspected menubarcommandids.h: all command IDs are #define MI_Name "MI_Name" macros. No MI_PreviewThis exists. MI_Preview (line 52) is the render preview command — unrelated.

Inspected MainWindow::defineActions() in mainwindow.cpp: each shortcuttable command is registered via createMenuXsheetAction(MI_Id, name, defaultShortcut, iconSVGName) which calls createAction() → CommandManager::define(). This is what makes commands appear in ShortcutPopup.

Inspected RowArea::contextMenuEvent(): "Preview This" at line 1367 is created with menu->addAction(tr("Preview This")) and connected to SLOT(onPreviewThis()). In contrast, commands like MI_InsertSceneFrame at line 1384 use cmdManager->getAction(MI_InsertSceneFrame) — which is why those show shortcut labels in the menu and are configurable.

Inspected onPreviewThis() at line 1534: it reads m_row (set during contextMenuEvent based on mouse position), then calls setPlayRange(m_row, m_row, step). For a global shortcut handler, we should use getCurrentFrame()->getFrame() instead.

Identified the MenuItemHandler pattern (menubarcommand.h:235): constructor takes CommandId, which auto-registers with CommandManager::setHandler(). The execute() virtual method is called when the command is triggered. Many xsheet commands like InsertSceneFrameCommand follow this pattern (xsheetcmd.cpp).
Documented findings in this meta task. Key insight: the only thing preventing "Preview This" from being shortcuttable is that it was never registered with CommandManager. The fix involves 4 files.

output.file: Reusable context on how OpenToonz shortcut system works.

phase.description: Add MI_PreviewThis as a registered command, create a global handler, and update the context menu to use it.

input.file: Target for registering MI_PreviewThis in defineActions().
Target for: (a) adding MenuItemHandler subclass, (b) updating contextMenuEvent to use cmdManager->getAction().

steps.step: Add #define MI_PreviewThis "MI_PreviewThis" to menubarcommandids.h, near the existing preview-related defines (around line 52-58).

In MainWindow::defineActions() in mainwindow.cpp, register MI_PreviewThis using createMenuXsheetAction(MI_PreviewThis, QT_TR_NOOP("Preview This"), "", ""). Place it near the existing xsheet commands (around line 2249-2260).

In RowArea::contextMenuEvent() in xshrowviewer.cpp, replace the local QAction creation: QAction *previewThis = menu->addAction(tr("Preview This")); connect(previewThis, SIGNAL(triggered()), SLOT(onPreviewThis())); with: menu->addAction(cmdManager->getAction(MI_PreviewThis)); This will show the shortcut label in the context menu and use the registered command handler when triggered.
NOTE: Since the global handler uses getCurrentFrame() instead of m_row, the behavior when triggered from the context menu will use the current frame (which is set when you click on a row). This is consistent because right-clicking a row also sets the current frame to that row first. Keep onPreviewThis() as a fallback if needed, but it may become unused.

Verify all files compile by checking includes and that MI_PreviewThis is accessible from all source files that reference it. Ensure menubarcommandids.h is included in both mainwindow.cpp and xshrowviewer.cpp.

Task profile: change Risk level: low Execution mode: standard-xml Execution autonomy: autonomous Approval mode: autonomous-gated Design guidance: not-needed
Key design decision: The global shortcut handler will use getCurrentFrame()->getFrame() instead of the context-menu m_row. This is correct because: (a) When navigating the xsheet, the current frame follows cursor position. (b) The user's workflow is: navigate to a frame → press shortcut → both markers set. (c) When right-clicking in the row area, the current frame is already set to that row by the mouse press event before the context menu appears.
The context menu's "Preview This" action will be replaced with the registered command. This means it will use the command's global handler instead of onPreviewThis(). Since right-clicking sets the current frame, the behavior is equivalent.
Note: The cmdManager variable in contextMenuEvent() is declared at line 1377. The "Preview This" action is currently at line 1367 (before cmdManager is declared). When switching to cmdManager->getAction(MI_PreviewThis), we must move it after line 1377 or declare cmdManager earlier. The simplest approach is to move the Preview This entry to after the existing cmdManager declaration.
